candidats.titre: File:Canny Burn (tributary of Tweed) culvert pipe Chester Crane Camp.jpg
candidats.description: Canny Burn, a minor tributary of the River Tweed, at the point where it emerges from its concrete pipe culvert. The upper portion of the Canny Burn glen was filled in and the stream confined in its culvert to facilitate the construction of the (now dismantled) Victorian railway line - of which a sturdy, but truncated, masonry arch still stands. Canny Burn flows down to the Tweed through a small, steep-sided and thickly-wooded glen in the South bank of the River Tweed, not far upstream from the busy road bridge that carries the A1 over the river on the outskirts of Berwick-upon-Tweed.
